message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **federal Canadian public holidays that create a “long weekend”** in 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the next weekday is usually observed, giving you a 3‑day break.)

| Holiday | Calendar date (2023) | Observed (if shifted) | Long‑weekend span |
|---------|----------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | Monday Jan 2 | **Sat Jan 1 – Mon Jan 3** |
| Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Monday Feb 20 | — | **Sun Feb 18 – Mon Feb 20** |
| Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | — | **Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9** |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | — | **Sun May 20 – Mon May 22** |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | Monday Jul 3 | **Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3** |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | — | **Sun Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4** |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | — | **Sun Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9** |
| Remembrance Day | Friday Nov 11 | — | **Fri Nov 10 – Sun Nov 12** |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | — | **Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25** |
| Boxing Day | Tuesday Dec 26 | — | **Tue Dec 26 – Thu Dec 28** |

> **Quick note:**  
> - Some provinces have additional statutory holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in BC, etc.).  
> - If you’re targeting a specific province, double‑check that province’s holiday calendar for any extra long weekends.

Feel free to copy/paste this table into your holiday‑planning app!
